stages.name: PyPDFLoader
stages.explain: Loads raw documents (PDF, web pages, files) and turns them into text plus metadata.

stages.name: RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter
stages.explain: Chunking. Cuts long text into overlapping pieces small enough to embed and to fit in the prompt. chunk_size is the piece length, chunk_overlap repeats the end of one chunk at the start of the next so a sentence is not lost at the cut.

stages.name: HuggingFaceEmbeddings
stages.explain: Embedding model. Turns each chunk (and later the question) into a vector of numbers so that similar meaning means nearby vectors.

stages.name: Chroma.from_documents
stages.explain: Vector store. Keeps every chunk's vector with its text and metadata, indexed (often HNSW) for fast nearest-neighbour search.

stages.name: BM25Retriever.from_documents
stages.explain: BM25 is keyword search. It scores chunks by how often the query words appear in them, discounted by how common those words are everywhere. It finds exact names and codes that embeddings miss.

stages.name: as_retriever
stages.explain: Retriever. Embeds the question and returns the k chunks whose vectors are closest (top-k).

stages.name: EnsembleRetriever
stages.explain: Fusion merges two ranked lists (dense vectors and BM25 keywords) into one. Reciprocal Rank Fusion gives each chunk 1/(60 + rank) from every list and adds them up, so chunks that rank well in both win.

stages.name: CrossEncoder
stages.explain: Reranker (cross-encoder). Reads the question and each candidate chunk together and scores how well they match. Slower than vector search but much more precise, so it re-orders the top-k candidates and keeps the best top-n.

stages.name: ChatPromptTemplate.from_messages
stages.explain: Prompt template. Puts the instructions, the retrieved chunks and the question into the text the model will read.

stages.name: StateGraph
stages.explain: A router (decision step). After a node runs, a function looks at the state and picks the next node, for example "call a tool again" or "finish". This is what turns a straight pipeline into a loop.

stages.name: add_conditional_edges
stages.explain: A router (decision step). After a node runs, a function looks at the state and picks the next node, for example "call a tool again" or "finish". This is what turns a straight pipeline into a loop.

stages.name: ChatOllama
stages.explain: Language model call. Reads the prompt and generates the answer token by token; with tools enabled it can answer with a tool call instead.

stages.name: LLM
stages.explain: Language model call. Reads the prompt and generates the answer token by token; with tools enabled it can answer with a tool call instead.

stages.name: generate
stages.explain: Language model call. Reads the prompt and generates the answer token by token; with tools enabled it can answer with a tool call instead.

stages.name: search_book
stages.explain: Tool. A function the model may ask to run (search, calculator, database query). Its result is fed back to the model.

stages.name: bind_tools
stages.explain: Agent loop. The model chooses a tool, the tool runs, the result goes back to the model, and this repeats until the model decides it is done.

stages.name: Block
stages.explain: A transformer block: attention (tokens look at each other) then an MLP (each token is transformed), each wrapped in a residual connection and normalization.

stages.name: CausalSelfAttention
stages.explain: A custom attention module: projects tokens to queries, keys and values and mixes values by softmax(QK^T / sqrt(d)). During generation its keys and values are what the KV cache stores.

stages.name: Embedding
stages.explain: Neural network layer defined in code.

stages.name: LayerNorm
stages.explain: Neural network layer defined in code.

stages.name: Linear
stages.explain: Neural network layer defined in code.

stages.name: MLP
stages.explain: The feed-forward (MLP) part of a transformer block: two linear layers with a non-linearity, applied to each token on its own.

stages.name: MultiheadAttention
stages.explain: Attention. Every token makes a query, key and value vector; each token's output is a weighted mix of the other tokens' values, weighted by softmax(query . key / sqrt(d)). Multi-head attention runs several of these in parallel.

stages.name: TinyGPT
stages.explain: A custom neural network module (nn.Module): its forward() defines how input tensors flow through the layers.

libraries.name: LangChain
libraries.explain: Building blocks for LLM apps: prompts, chat models, retrievers, tools, chains wired together with the | operator (LCEL).

libraries.name: LangGraph
libraries.explain: Builds agents as a state machine graph: nodes are steps, conditional edges are decisions, and the state is checkpointed between steps.

libraries.name: vLLM
libraries.explain: High-throughput serving with PagedAttention, continuous batching and prefix caching.

libraries.name: PyTorch
libraries.explain: Tensors on CPU/GPU with autograd; nn.Module layers; the base of most ML code.

libraries.name: Open Knowledge Format (OKF)
libraries.explain: Google Cloud's vendor-neutral format (2026) for agent knowledge: a folder of Markdown files with YAML frontmatter (a required `type` field), plus reserved index.md and log.md files.

libraries.name: FastAPI
libraries.explain: Python web API framework; routes are typed functions validated with Pydantic.

libraries.name: React
libraries.explain: Builds UIs from components; re-renders when state changes.

libraries.name: Redis
libraries.explain: In-memory key-value store used for caches, queues and pub/sub.

memoryTechniques.name: KV cache quantization
memoryTechniques.explain: Stores keys and values in 8-bit (or 4-bit) instead of 16-bit, roughly halving KV cache memory so longer contexts fit, at a small accuracy cost.

memoryTechniques.name: Model residency (keep_alive) and context size
memoryTechniques.explain: keep_alive decides how long Ollama keeps the model loaded in RAM/VRAM after a request. num_ctx sets the context length, which sizes the KV cache.

memoryTechniques.name: Capped history in Redis (rolling buffer)
memoryTechniques.explain: Pushes each new item onto a Redis list and trims it to the last N, so the list works as a ring buffer. Used for chat history, memory per conversation stays fixed however long it runs, and every API worker sees the same history because it lives in the Redis container, not in the process.

memoryTechniques.name: Response cache with expiry (TTL)
memoryTechniques.explain: Stores a computed result under a key with a time-to-live. A repeat request reads the stored copy instead of recomputing; Redis deletes the key when the TTL runs out, and its maxmemory policy evicts old keys when it is full.

memoryTechniques.name: PagedAttention KV cache
memoryTechniques.explain: vLLM stores the KV cache in fixed-size blocks (pages) like an OS stores memory in pages. A request's cache does not need one contiguous slab, so almost no memory is wasted and many requests fit at once. gpu_memory_utilization sets how much of the GPU vLLM may claim.

memoryTechniques.name: Automatic prefix caching
memoryTechniques.explain: When two prompts start with the same tokens (same system prompt, same document), vLLM reuses the KV blocks it already computed for that prefix instead of recomputing them. Time-to-first-token drops for repeated prefixes.

services.name: web
services.explain: Frontend built from this repository (1 source file): the screens the user sees in the browser.

services.name: proxy
services.explain: nginx reverse proxy: serves the built frontend and forwards /api calls to the backend.

services.name: api
services.explain: Backend API built from this repository (8 source files): receives HTTP requests and runs the app logic.

services.name: ollama
services.explain: Ollama model server. Loads GGUF models into RAM/VRAM and answers chat and embedding requests over HTTP on port 11434. A model stays loaded for 10m after its last request. Up to 4 requests share one loaded model, each with its own KV cache.

services.name: chroma
services.explain: Chroma vector store running as a server: collections of embeddings with metadata filters.

services.name: cache
services.explain: Redis in-memory key-value store: caches, sessions, rate limits, queues. Redis Stack adds vector search. It may hold 256mb of data; when full it evicts keys by the allkeys-lru policy.

memoryMap.explain: Every token being generated keeps a key and a value per layer; this cache grows with the context and is freed when the request ends.
LLM loads the whole model into GPU memory of api and keeps it there.
KV blocks for a prefix many prompts share stay in GPU memory and are reused until space is needed.
While a reply is generated the model keeps a key and a value per token per layer; the context size decides how big this gets.
The chat model is loaded into GPU memory by Ollama, not into the API process; the API only sends HTTP requests.
BM25Retriever.from_documents holds the word counts for every chunk in api's RAM; it is rebuilt when the process restarts.
HuggingFaceEmbeddings loads the model into RAM when it is created and keeps it there for the life of the process.
CrossEncoder loads the model into RAM when it is created and keeps it there for the life of the process.

chroma keeps the search graph and the vectors it walks in RAM so a query touches a few hundred vectors in milliseconds.
